projects.title: Real-time Crypto Price Dashboard
projects.summary: Build a live-updating market dashboard with a sortable watchlist and price chart.
projects.brief:
Northwind Trading wants an internal dashboard for traders to watch a handful of crypto pairs. You will consume the public Coinbase Exchange WebSocket feed (wss://ws-feed.exchange.coinbase.com, channel `ticker`, products such as BTC-USD, ETH-USD, SOL-USD) and the REST candles endpoint (`/products/{id}/candles?granularity=60`) for history.

The main screen shows a watchlist table (symbol, last price, 24h change %, volume) that updates as ticks arrive, plus a detail panel with a 1-hour candlestick or line chart for the selected pair. Traders keep this open all day on a second monitor, so it must not leak memory, must reconnect after network loss and must stay responsive when ticks arrive several times per second.

You may choose any chart library. Design is secondary to clarity: price changes should be visually obvious (flash or colour) without being distracting, and the layout must work from 1024px wide up.
requirements: Subscribe to the ticker channel for at least 5 products and update rows in place
Sortable columns (symbol, price, change %) with sort state kept while ticks arrive
Selected pair shows a chart seeded from REST candles and extended live from ticks
Automatic reconnect with exponential backoff and a visible connection-status indicator
Throttle or batch rendering so the UI stays smooth at 10+ updates per second
Add and remove pairs from the watchlist, persisted in localStorage
Loading, empty and error states for every async view
Unit tests for the data-normalisation and sort logic plus at least one component test
stretch: Playwright smoke test of the happy path
deliverables: Public Git repository with a meaningful commit history
README covering setup, run and test commands, design decisions and known trade-offs

rubric.description: Live updates match the feed, change % is computed correctly, reconnect works after the socket is killed
Typed message models, small components, no stray any, clean hooks with proper cleanup
Feed handling separated from UI, state updates batched, sensible state ownership
No unnecessary re-renders, no leaked sockets or timers, profiler evidence or reasoning in README
Meaningful tests of pure logic and one UI behaviour; not snapshot-only
Clear status states, colour is not the only change signal, semantic table markup
Setup, decisions and trade-offs are easy to follow

projects.title: Accessible Component Library
projects.summary: Create a small themeable component library with documentation and accessibility guarantees.
projects.brief:
Brightside Health is consolidating three web apps onto one design system. They need a first release of a React component library covering Button, TextField, Select (listbox pattern), Modal Dialog, Tabs and Toast, with theming through CSS variables and a Storybook (or equivalent) documentation site.

Accessibility is the primary acceptance criterion: components must follow the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices patterns, be fully keyboard operable, trap and restore focus in dialogs, announce toasts through a live region and meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast in both themes. Visual polish matters less than correctness of behaviour.

The library will be published to a private npm registry, so treat the public API as a contract: props must be typed, components must forward refs and spread native attributes, and the build must output ESM and CJS with type declarations and tree-shakeable exports.
requirements: Six components with typed props and ref forwarding
Light and dark themes driven purely by CSS custom properties
Dialog traps focus, closes on Escape and restores focus to the trigger
Select supports type-ahead, arrow-key navigation and aria-activedescendant
Tabs support automatic and manual activation modes
Toast queue announced via aria-live with configurable duration and pause on hover
Interaction tests with Testing Library and automated axe checks per component
Build outputs ESM, CJS and .d.ts files; package.json exports map is correct
stretch: Controlled and uncontrolled modes for every input component
deliverables: Public Git repository with a meaningful commit history
README covering setup, run and test commands, design decisions and known trade-offs

rubric.description: Correct roles, states, focus management, keyboard maps and contrast, verified by tests not only claims
Components behave as documented in controlled and uncontrolled use
Consistent props, composability, forwardRef, sensible defaults, minimal surprise
Strict TypeScript, no duplication between components, clear hooks
Behavioural tests with Testing Library plus axe; edge cases such as nested dialogs
Stories show each state, docs explain accessibility behaviour and theming
Working exports map, treeshaking, types published

projects.title: Offline-first Kanban Board
projects.summary: Build a drag-and-drop task board that persists locally and works offline.
projects.brief:
A small agency wants a lightweight Kanban board for their own use. Users can create columns (To do, Doing, Done by default), add cards with a title and optional description, and drag cards between and within columns. Everything must persist in the browser so a refresh never loses work.

The agency is not asking for accounts or a backend. They care that the board is quick, that drag and drop also works with the keyboard, and that the code is simple enough that a junior teammate can extend it next quarter.

Seed data is not provided; the first-run experience should create the three default columns and one example card.
requirements: Create, rename and delete columns
Create, edit and delete cards
Drag cards between and within columns, order is preserved
Keyboard alternative for moving cards (for example buttons or key shortcuts)
State persisted to localStorage and restored on load
Basic search box filtering cards by title
Responsive layout that scrolls horizontally on narrow screens
Tests covering the reducer or state-management logic

projects.title: URL Shortener with Analytics API
projects.summary: Build a production-minded URL shortening service with click analytics and rate limiting.
projects.brief:
LinkLoop needs a REST service that creates short links, redirects visitors and reports click statistics. A client posts `POST /api/links {"url": "https://example.com/long", "alias": "optional", "expires_at": "ISO-8601 optional"}` and receives a short code. `GET /{code}` redirects with 302 (or 404 / 410 for unknown or expired codes).

Every redirect must be recorded (timestamp, user-agent family, referrer host, country if you can derive it cheaply). `GET /api/links/{code}/stats?from=&to=&interval=day` returns total clicks and a time series. Redirect latency is the key metric: the p95 target is under 30ms on a single instance at 500 req/s, so recording clicks must not block the response.

Authentication is by API key header for the management endpoints. Redirects are public. Use a real database (PostgreSQL preferred) and provide migrations.
requirements: Create links with random 7-character base62 codes, collision-safe, or a user alias with validation
Reject invalid URLs and dangerous schemes (javascript:, data:)
Redirect endpoint with 302, 404 and 410 handling
Click events recorded asynchronously (queue, background task or batched insert)
Stats endpoint with date range and day/hour bucketing
API key auth on management endpoints, per-key rate limiting (for example 60 requests/min) returning 429 with Retry-After
Database migrations and an index strategy explained in the README
Automated tests for creation, redirect, expiry, rate limit and stats
stretch: Load test script with results (k6 or wrk)
deliverables: Public Git repository with a meaningful commit history

docker-compose.yml that starts the service and database

projects.title: Double-entry Payments Ledger
projects.summary: Design an idempotent, auditable ledger service that never loses or invents money.
projects.brief:
A fintech start-up needs the core of its wallet product: a ledger service that records transfers between accounts using double-entry bookkeeping. Every transfer creates two or more immutable entries that sum to zero per currency. Balances are derived from entries, but a materialised balance must be available with strong consistency for authorisation checks.

The API exposes `POST /transfers` (with an `Idempotency-Key` header), `GET /accounts/{id}/balance` and `GET /accounts/{id}/entries?cursor=`. Clients retry aggressively and several requests for the same account arrive concurrently, so you must prevent overdrafts under concurrency, prevent double-processing on retries, and make partial failure impossible.

You are free to choose the stack but must use a relational database with real transactions. Include a concurrency test that fires at least 200 parallel transfers against two accounts and asserts that the invariants hold afterwards.
requirements: Accounts with currency and optional overdraft policy
Immutable entries, no updates or deletes, enforced at database level where possible
Transfers atomically create balanced entries and update materialised balances
Idempotency keys: same key and payload returns the original result, same key with different payload returns 409
Concurrency control that prevents overdrafts (row locks, serialisable isolation or equivalent) with the choice justified
Cursor-based pagination of entries
Money stored as integer minor units, never floats; reject cross-currency transfers without an explicit FX entry
Concurrency and property-style tests asserting global sum is zero and no balance goes below the allowed limit
A reconciliation endpoint or script that recomputes balances from entries and reports drift
stretch: Audit log with hash chaining of entries
Multi-currency transfers via an FX account
deliverables: Public Git repository with a meaningful commit history
README covering setup, run and test commands, design decisions and known trade-offs
tech: Go or Java or TypeScript or Python

rubric.description: Invariants hold: zero-sum entries, no overdraft, idempotent retries
Transaction boundaries, isolation choice and schema constraints are justified
Domain model separated from transport, money type, clear errors
Real concurrency tests, idempotency and failure-injection tests
Input validation, no sensitive data in logs, safe error messages

projects.title: Event-driven Notification Service
projects.summary: Build a service that fans out notifications to email, SMS and webhook channels with retries.
projects.brief:
A SaaS product emits events such as `invoice.paid` or `user.invited`. A notification service must accept them via `POST /events`, look up each user's channel preferences and templates, and deliver through pluggable channel adapters (email, SMS, webhook). Real providers are not required; implement fake adapters that randomly fail 20% of the time so your retry logic is exercised.

Delivery must be at-least-once with de-duplication so users never see the same notification twice, and one failing channel must not block others. Failed deliveries retry with exponential backoff and jitter up to 5 attempts, then land in a dead-letter list that operators can inspect and replay through an admin endpoint.

Expose basic observability: structured logs with a correlation id, a `/metrics` endpoint (Prometheus format) with sent, failed and retried counters, and a `/health` endpoint.
requirements: Event ingestion endpoint with schema validation and 202 responses
Per-user channel preferences and per-event-type templates with variable substitution
Worker consuming from a durable queue (Redis, RabbitMQ, SQS-compatible or database-backed)
Channel adapter interface with at least three fake implementations
Retry with exponential backoff and jitter, dead-letter storage, replay endpoint
Idempotent delivery keyed by event id + channel + recipient
Prometheus metrics and structured logging with correlation ids
Tests for retry timing, dedupe and failure isolation
stretch: Graceful shutdown that drains in-flight jobs
deliverables: Public Git repository with a meaningful commit history
README covering setup, run and test commands, design decisions and known trade-offs

rubric.description: Events delivered once per channel, retries and DLQ behave as specified
Clean adapter interface, durable queue, separation of API and workers
Readable modules, typed events, configuration via env
Failure isolation, graceful shutdown, backoff with jitter
Deterministic tests for time-based retry logic, dedupe tests

projects.title: Appointment Booking Platform
projects.summary: Build a booking app where customers reserve time slots with double-booking prevention.
projects.brief:
Glow Studio, a salon with five stylists, wants online booking. Customers pick a service (30, 60 or 90 minutes), a stylist (or 'any') and an available slot, then confirm with name and email. Stylists have weekly working hours and may have days off. Seed five stylists, six services and Monday to Saturday hours of 09:00 to 18:00.

The critical rule is that two customers must never hold the same stylist at overlapping times, even when they click Confirm at the same moment. The studio is in one time zone but customers travel, so slots display in the studio's zone with a clear label and are stored in UTC.

A simple admin view (basic auth or a seeded login is fine) lists the day's bookings and lets staff cancel one. Confirmation emails can be logged to the console.

Availability endpoint returning free slots for a date, service and optional stylist

stretch: Reminder emails via a scheduled job

rubric.description: No double bookings, correct slot generation across edges such as end of day

projects.title: Real-time Team Chat
projects.summary: Build channel-based chat with presence, typing indicators and message history.
projects.brief:
Relay is an internal chat tool for a 200-person company. Users sign in (email + password is enough), join public channels and exchange messages in real time. Messages persist and load with infinite scroll upward. Presence (online/offline) and typing indicators are shown per channel.

The backend must work across more than one server process, so a message sent to instance A reaches subscribers on instance B (use Redis pub/sub or a similar broker). Messages must arrive in order per channel, survive a page refresh and not be duplicated when the client reconnects and resends.

Provide a Docker Compose set-up that runs two backend instances behind a simple reverse proxy so reviewers can verify cross-instance delivery.

projects.title: Personal Expense Tracker
projects.summary: Build a small CRUD app for tracking expenses with category totals and CSV export.
projects.brief:
A freelancer asks for a simple web app to record expenses. Each expense has an amount, currency (single currency is fine), date, category and optional note. Users register, log in and see only their own data.

The dashboard shows the current month's total, a breakdown by category and the ten most recent expenses. A filter bar limits the list by date range and category, and a button exports the filtered list as CSV.

Keep it simple and well-tested: the client wants something they can host cheaply, so SQLite is acceptable, and a single deployable unit is a plus.

projects.title: Habit Tracker with Streaks
projects.summary: Build a cross-platform habit tracker with local storage, streaks and daily reminders.
projects.brief:
A wellness start-up wants a prototype habit tracker. Users add habits (name, colour, target days of the week), tick them off each day and see current and longest streaks. Data is local to the device; there is no backend.

Streak logic is where bugs hide: a habit scheduled Monday, Wednesday, Friday keeps its streak across Tuesday and Thursday, a missed scheduled day resets it, and changing the device time zone must not corrupt history. Daily reminders fire at a user-chosen time via local notifications.

The app should feel native, support both light and dark mode and be usable with large system font sizes.

projects.title: Offline-first Field Inspection App
projects.summary: Build a mobile app that collects inspection forms offline and syncs reliably when online.
projects.brief:
A utilities company sends inspectors to remote sites with poor connectivity. The app downloads assigned inspections (`GET /api/inspections?updated_since=`), lets the inspector fill checklists, take photos and add notes offline, and uploads results when a connection returns. You will build the app and a small mock API to sync with.

Sync is the hard part. Edits made offline must never be lost, uploads must be resumable and idempotent (the network may drop mid-upload), and conflicts (the office edited the same inspection) must be detected using a version field and surfaced to the user rather than silently overwritten.

The app must remain usable on a 3-year-old mid-range phone: photos are compressed before upload and large lists are virtualised.

projects.title: Live Ride Tracking Screen
projects.summary: Implement a ride-tracking map screen with smooth marker animation and ETA updates.
projects.brief:
A ride-hailing client needs the rider-side tracking screen. A mock location feed (provided by you as a WebSocket or polling server) emits driver coordinates every 2 seconds along a route, plus status changes: `searching`, `driver_assigned`, `arriving`, `in_trip`, `completed`.

The map shows pickup, destination and the driver's marker, which must move smoothly between updates, rotate towards its heading and never jump backwards. A bottom sheet shows driver details, vehicle, ETA and a cancel action that is only available before `in_trip`.

Handle real-world mess: GPS updates arrive out of order or duplicated, the app goes to background and returns, and connectivity drops for ten seconds. The screen must recover cleanly.

projects.title: Customer Support RAG Assistant
projects.summary: Build a retrieval-augmented question answering service with citations and an evaluation harness.
projects.brief:
HelpDesk Co. has 300 markdown help-centre articles and wants an assistant that answers customer questions using only those articles, with citations. You may use any open or hosted embedding model and LLM; the grader will run your code with their own API key via environment variables, so no keys in the repo. Use a public documentation set (for example a project's docs) if you do not have articles of your own, and say which in the README.

Build an ingestion script that chunks documents (justify chunk size and overlap), embeds them and stores vectors (FAISS, Chroma, pgvector or similar). Expose `POST /ask {"question": "..."}` returning `{"answer": ..., "sources": [{"doc": ..., "chunk": ..., "score": ...}]}`. If retrieved context does not support an answer, the service must say it does not know instead of guessing.

The differentiator is evaluation. Write 25 or more question/expected-source pairs (a golden set), measure retrieval hit rate@k and a simple answer-faithfulness check, and report numbers plus at least one experiment (for example chunk size or reranking) showing what improved.

Vector store with top-k retrieval and optional metadata filters
HTTP endpoint returning answer and source citations
Prompt that restricts answers to retrieved context and returns an explicit refusal when evidence is missing
Golden set of 25+ questions including 5 unanswerable ones

stretch: Hybrid search (BM25 plus vectors) with reranking

projects.title: Churn Prediction Service
projects.summary: Train, evaluate and serve a customer churn classifier from tabular data.
projects.brief:
A subscription business gives you a CSV of 7,000 customers with columns such as tenure, monthly charges, contract type, support tickets and a binary `churned` label (use the public Telco Customer Churn dataset if you do not have one). Your job is to produce a model the retention team can trust and a small API to score new customers.

The team cares more about sound methodology than a fancy algorithm. Avoid leakage, split data correctly, choose metrics suited to class imbalance and explain what the model learned. A logistic regression baseline is required before anything more complex.

Finally wrap the best model in a service: `POST /predict` accepts one customer JSON and returns a churn probability and the top three contributing features.

projects.title: Tool-using LLM Agent with Evals
projects.summary: Build a function-calling agent for a booking domain and a regression test suite to measure it.
projects.brief:
A travel start-up wants an LLM agent that helps users change flights. The agent has four tools backed by a mock service you write: `search_flights`, `get_booking`, `change_booking` and `escalate_to_human`. Policy: changes within 24 hours of departure are not allowed, fare differences above 200 EUR need explicit user confirmation, and the agent never reveals other customers' bookings.

Implement the agent loop yourself (do not rely on a framework's black-box agent executor): maintain message history, parse tool calls, validate arguments against JSON schemas, execute tools, handle tool errors and cap iterations and spend. Trace every run to a JSONL file with prompts, tool calls, latency and token counts.

Then build the evaluation suite: at least 30 scripted scenarios (happy path, policy violations, ambiguous requests, adversarial prompt injection in a booking note, tool failures). Score with deterministic checks first (final state of the mock DB, tools called) and an LLM-judge only for tone. Report pass rates and iterate on prompts or tools, documenting what changed.

projects.title: A/B Test Analysis and Recommendation
projects.summary: Analyse an experiment, check validity, and write a decision memo for stakeholders.
projects.brief:
An e-commerce team ran a checkout redesign for three weeks. You receive `assignments.csv` (user_id, variant, assigned_at, platform, country) and `events.csv` (user_id, event, timestamp, revenue). Generate a realistic synthetic dataset yourself if you do not have one: roughly 120,000 users, 50/50 split, baseline conversion near 4.2% and a small true lift.

Before looking at the result, validate the experiment: check sample ratio mismatch, balance of covariates across variants, novelty effects over time and instrumentation problems such as duplicate events or users in both arms. Then estimate the effect on conversion and revenue per user with confidence intervals, using appropriate tests (and a bootstrap for the skewed revenue metric).

Deliver a notebook and a one-page decision memo for a product manager with no statistics background: ship, do not ship or extend the test, and why.

projects.title: Retail Demand Forecasting
projects.summary: Forecast daily SKU-level demand with proper time-series validation and prediction intervals.
projects.brief:
A grocery chain wants 14-day demand forecasts for 50 SKUs across 10 stores. The data has daily unit sales, price, promotion flag, weather and holiday calendar columns (the public M5 or Store Item Demand datasets are acceptable substitutes). Many series are intermittent with zero-sales days, and promotions cause large spikes.

Set up honest evaluation first: rolling-origin cross-validation with a 14-day horizon, never random splits. Compare at least three approaches: a seasonal naive baseline, a classical model (ETS or ARIMA, or Prophet) and a gradient-boosted model with lag and calendar features. Report MASE or WAPE per segment, not only an overall average.

The business also needs uncertainty: produce 80% prediction intervals and report their empirical coverage on the backtest. Finish with a short analysis of where forecasts fail and what extra data would help.
requirements: Data loading with checks for gaps, negative values and stockouts masquerading as zero demand
Rolling-origin backtest harness reusable across models
Seasonal naive baseline plus two or more additional models

projects.title: Daily Sales ETL Pipeline
projects.summary: Build an idempotent batch pipeline that loads raw sales files into a warehouse star schema.
projects.brief:
A retailer drops CSV files into an `incoming/` folder every night: `orders_YYYYMMDD.csv`, `order_items_YYYYMMDD.csv` and `customers_YYYYMMDD.csv`. You must load them into a warehouse (PostgreSQL, DuckDB or BigQuery emulator) as a star schema with `fact_order_items`, `dim_customer` (type 2 slowly changing on address) and `dim_date`.

The pipeline must be idempotent: re-running a day's load must not duplicate rows, and re-processing a corrected file must update facts correctly. Bad rows go to a quarantine table with a reason rather than failing the whole batch, and a data-quality report shows row counts, null rates and rejected-row counts per run.

Orchestrate with Airflow, Prefect, Dagster or a well-structured CLI with a scheduler config. Provide a data generator so reviewers can run 7 simulated days.

projects.summary: Write scripts that back up a database and files to object storage, verify them and test restores.
projects.brief:

projects.brief:
A client needs an authentication microservice for several internal apps. Implement registration, login, logout, password reset by email token and TOTP-based multi-factor authentication. The focus is security detail. Add rate limiting and progressive lockout against credential stuffing, detect refresh-token reuse and revoke the whole token family, and set cookie flags and CSRF protection correctly.

Write a threat model (STRIDE or attack tree) and automated tests that act as the attacker: brute force, token replay, session fixation, timing differences and enumeration.

A second command parses `requirements.txt` or `package-lock.json` and checks versions against a small local advisory file (JSON you define) and reports affected packages with fixed versions.

A user pastes an Ethereum address and sees a portfolio overview. Using a public JSON-RPC provider (Alchemy, Infura, public endpoints) or an explorer API, show the ETH balance, balances for a configurable list of ERC-20 tokens (USDC, DAI, WETH), and the last 20 transactions with direction, counterparty, value and timestamp.

Prices come from a public price API such as CoinGecko; show total portfolio value in USD with a clear note when prices are cached or unavailable. The app is strictly read-only: no private keys, no signing. Handle addresses properly: validate checksums, accept ENS names, and treat unreadable data gracefully.

Write the data-access layer carefully. Token balances need correct decimals handling with BigInt or a decimal library, never JavaScript floats.

projects.title: 2D Platformer Vertical Slice
projects.summary: Build one polished level of a 2D platformer with tight controls and enemies.
projects.brief:
An indie studio wants a vertical slice to test their game feel. Using Unity, Godot or a web engine such as Phaser, deliver one level with a player character that runs, jumps with variable height, double jumps, has coyote time and jump buffering, and can collect coins and reach an exit. Two enemy types (a patroller and a shooter) and one hazard type should exist.

Control feel is the main criterion, so expose tuning values (gravity, jump velocity, acceleration, coyote window) in a configuration file or inspector, and document the numbers you chose and why. Physics must be frame-rate independent and behave identically at 30, 60 and 144 FPS.

Include a main menu, pause, a HUD (health, coins), restart on death, simple audio and a game-state architecture that does not depend on global singletons everywhere. Unit-test the pure logic such as scoring and state transitions.
requirements: Player controller with variable jump height, coyote time and jump buffering
Frame-rate independent movement (fixed timestep or delta-time correct)
Two enemy types with distinct behaviours and a hazard
Collectibles, score and a level exit with win state

projects.title: Authoritative Multiplayer Arena Prototype
projects.summary: Build a server-authoritative 2D arena shooter with client prediction and lag compensation.
projects.brief:
A studio is evaluating netcode skills. Build a top-down arena where 4 to 8 players move and shoot, using a server-authoritative model: clients send inputs, the server simulates at a fixed 30 Hz tick and broadcasts snapshots. Cheating (speed hacks, teleporting, rapid fire) must be impossible by construction because the server validates and simulates everything.

To keep movement responsive under 100 ms latency, implement client-side prediction with server reconciliation for the local player, and entity interpolation for remote players. Shots use simple lag compensation: the server rewinds target positions to the shooter's view time within a limit before hit-testing.

Provide a network simulator (configurable latency, jitter and packet loss) and demonstrate the system staying playable at 120 ms, 5% loss. Include automated headless tests where bots connect and play, asserting determinism of the simulation and bounded divergence between client prediction and server state.
requirements: Fixed-timestep server simulation with input queues and snapshots
Binary or compact message protocol with sequence numbers and acknowledgements
Client prediction and reconciliation for the local player
Remote entity interpolation with a jitter buffer
Server-side validation of movement and fire rate
Lag-compensated hit detection with a rewind cap

Headless bot tests proving determinism and bounded error

projects.title: Procedural Dungeon Generator
projects.summary: Generate playable dungeons procedurally with seeds, connectivity guarantees and a pathfinding demo.
projects.brief:
A roguelike team needs a dungeon generation library plus a small playable demo. Given a seed, width and height, it produces a grid-based dungeon with rooms, corridors, doors, a start, an exit and optional keys/locked doors. The same seed must always produce the same dungeon on every platform.

Every dungeon must be solvable: the exit is reachable from the start, keys appear before the doors they open, and no required item sits in an unreachable pocket. Use a documented algorithm (BSP, random walk with room placement, wave function collapse or cellular automata plus post-processing) and validate every output with an automated solver.

Provide a visual demo (browser canvas, terminal or engine view) where an agent navigates using A* to collect the key and reach the exit, plus a batch tool that generates 10,000 seeds and reports the failure rate, average generation time and distribution of room counts.

Configurable parameters (size, room count, loop density)

projects.title: Low-power Sensor Node Firmware
projects.summary: Write firmware that samples a sensor, filters data and reports reliably over MQTT.
projects.brief:
A greenhouse operator needs battery-powered nodes reporting temperature and humidity every 5 minutes. Target an ESP32, STM32 or Raspberry Pi Pico (or a simulator such as Wokwi or Renode if you have no hardware). A DHT22/BME280-style sensor is read over GPIO or I2C and values are published to an MQTT broker as JSON with a timestamp and node id.

Power and reliability dominate: sleep between samples (deep sleep or low-power mode) and wake only to measure and transmit. Readings must be filtered (median of several samples) to reject spikes, implausible values must be flagged, and messages must survive Wi-Fi outages by buffering up to 100 readings in flash or RAM and flushing in order on reconnect.

Separate hardware access from logic through a thin hardware-abstraction layer so the filtering, buffering and message formatting can be unit-tested on a desktop without a device.
requirements: Sensor driver behind an abstraction interface
Median filter and plausibility checks (range and rate of change)
MQTT client with QoS 1, last-will message and reconnect handling

stretch: TLS to the broker with certificate validation

README covering setup, run and test commands, design decisions and known trade-offs

projects.title: RTOS Motor and Safety Controller
projects.summary: Implement a multi-task RTOS controller with PID speed control, fault handling and a command interface.
projects.brief:
A small automation company wants control firmware for a DC motor with an encoder. Use FreeRTOS or Zephyr on an STM32/ESP32 target or a simulator with a motor model. Tasks: a 1 kHz control loop running PID speed control from encoder counts, a command task parsing a serial protocol (`SET RPM 1200`, `GET STATUS`, `STOP`), a telemetry task streaming status at 10 Hz and a supervisor monitoring faults.

Safety requirements are strict: overcurrent, stalled motor (commanded duty high but no encoder movement), command timeout (no valid command for 2 seconds) and watchdog expiry must all drive the output to a safe state within 10 ms. The control loop must meet deadlines, so avoid blocking calls, dynamic allocation and unbounded priority inversion (use mutexes with priority inheritance or lock-free queues).

Provide timing evidence: measured loop jitter, worst-case execution time and stack high-water marks per task. Test the PID and protocol parser on the host, and fault logic using injected faults in the simulator or a hardware-in-the-loop harness.
requirements: Task design document with priorities, periods and inter-task communication
PID with anti-windup, output clamping and tunable gains
Encoder speed estimation handling counter wraparound
Serial command parser with bounds checking and checksum or framing

Host unit tests for PID, parser and wraparound
Fault-injection tests for overcurrent, stall and timeout
Notes on how the design addresses priority inversion and race conditions

README covering setup, run and test commands, design decisions and known trade-offs

rubric.description: Control and fault behaviour meet specified timing and safe-state rules

projects.title: Smart Home IoT Gateway
projects.summary: Build a gateway bridging BLE/Zigbee-style devices to the cloud with secure provisioning.
projects.brief:
A smart-home start-up needs a gateway service for a Raspberry Pi class device. Simulated local devices (door sensors, smart plugs, thermostats) speak a simple local protocol over MQTT or BLE-like characteristics. The gateway discovers them, normalises their data into a common device model, forwards state to a cloud MQTT/HTTP endpoint and applies commands coming back.

Security is first-class: devices are onboarded through a provisioning flow that exchanges per-device credentials (no shared default passwords), cloud connections use TLS with certificate validation and device state is accepted only from enrolled identities. Commands from the cloud are authenticated and replay-protected.

The gateway must keep working when the internet is down: local automations (for example 'if door opens after 22:00, turn on hallway plug') run locally from a rules file, state is queued and synced on reconnect, and a local REST API exposes current status.

Local REST API with current device state

Tests for the rules engine, replay protection and offline queue

README covering setup, run and test commands, design decisions and known trade-offs
